test_cases.description: OpenAI investigation over ChatGPT shooting incident

source.title: Florida AG announces investigation into OpenAI over shooting that allegedly involved ChatGPT
source.summary: Florida's Attorney General announced an investigation into OpenAI over the alleged role of ChatGPT in a deadly shooting at Florida State University.
source.content: Florida's Attorney General, James Uthmeier, announced Thursday that his office planned to investigate OpenAI over the alleged role of ChatGPT in a deadly shooting last year. In April 2025, a gunman opened fire on Florida State University's campus, killing two and injuring five. Last week, attorneys for one of the victims of the shooting claimed that ChatGPT had been used to plan the attack. The family of the victim has said that they plan to sue OpenAI over the incident. "AI should advance mankind, not destroy it," Uthmeier said in a statement posted to X. "We're demanding answers on OpenAI's activities that have hurt kids, endangered Americans, and facilitated the recent FSU mass shooting. Wrongdoers must be held accountable." Uthmeier added in a video that subpoenas were "forthcoming" as part of the probe. ChatGPT has been linked to a growing number of deaths and violent incidents — including murders, suicides, and shootings — and has added to worries over the advent of what psychologists call "AI psychosis," delusions that are reinforced, encouraged, or deepened by communications with chatbots. For example, Stein-Erik Soelberg, a man with a history of mental health issues, had regularly communicated with ChatGPT before he killed his mother and then himself last year, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation. The chatbot frequently seemed to reinforce the paranoid thoughts that consumed him in the lead-up to the murder-suicide. When reached for comment by TechCrunch, an OpenAI spokesperson provided the following statement: "Each week, more than 900 million people use ChatGPT to improve their daily lives through uses such as learning new skills or navigating complex healthcare systems. Our ongoing safety work continues to play an important role in delivering these benefits to everyday people, as well as supporting scientific research and discovery. We build ChatGPT to understand people's intent and respond in a safe and appropriate way, and we continue improving our technology. We will cooperate with the Attorney General's investigation." Florida's probe continues a string of bad luck for OpenAI. A New Yorker profile on Sam Altman published earlier this week showed criticism and discontent within the company and among its investors, even quoting a Microsoft executive as saying: "I think there's a small but real chance he's eventually remembered as a Bernie Madoff- or Sam Bankman-Fried-level scammer." Meanwhile, a Stargate-related project in the United Kingdom had to be paused, reportedly due to high energy costs and regulation.

test_cases.description: Fubo mobile app update with sports highlights

source.title: Fubo's mobile app is pushing more sports highlights
source.summary: Fubo is rolling out a mobile app update with short-form videos, live video previews, and AI-generated highlight playlists.
source.content: Fubo is rolling out a big mobile app update today that adds a bunch of new features, including short-form videos with news about your favorite teams and leagues. You'll also find a carousel of live video as soon as you open the app, allowing you to preview games before you tap into them. The live TV streaming service is expanding a feature called Team Channels, which uses AI to create a playlist of bite-sized clips from a game that you've recorded. But Fubo is expanding this feature to more leagues (though the company doesn't say which ones), while its AI system can now pick up on more kinds of key moments to include in its playlist. Fubo, which merged with Hulu + Live TV last year, is likely rolling out these new features to stand out in an increasingly crowded sports streaming space. ESPN launched its dedicated streaming app with a TikTok-like video feed last year, while Fox, Comcast, DirecTV, and YouTube TV have rolled out sports-focused streaming packages of their own. Fubo launched a middle-of-the-road $55.99 per month sports streaming package last September. In the coming weeks, Fubo says you'll be able to watch Team Channels in portrait mode on the homepage, and Fubo's AI system will zoom "into the most critical areas of the video" — similar to NBC's Peacock vertical video streams. Fubo is making its game alerts available for baseball games starting today, too. That means you can receive push notifications about key updates in an MLB game, like a home run, and tap into the notification to jump to the exact moment. The service launched personalized game alerts for NBA games last year.
source.classification_reason: Primary: Mobile & Apps (app update). Secondary: Consumer Tech (streaming service).

source.title: OpenAI raises $6.6B in funding round led by Thrive Capital
source.summary: OpenAI has raised $6.6 billion in new funding at a $157 billion post-money valuation, led by Thrive Capital with participation from Microsoft, Nvidia, and SoftBank.
source.content: OpenAI announced on Wednesday that it has closed a $6.6 billion funding round, the largest venture capital deal in history, led by Thrive Capital. The round values the ChatGPT maker at $157 billion post-money. Microsoft, which has already invested more than $13 billion in OpenAI, participated again. Other notable investors include Nvidia, SoftBank, and Khosla Ventures. CEO Sam Altman said the funding will be used to push the boundaries of AI research and expand computing capacity. The company plans to restructure from a nonprofit to a for-profit benefit corporation within two years.
source.classification_reason: Primary: Startup (funding news). Secondary: AI (OpenAI company).

source.title: Apple announces M4 chip with 3nm process technology
source.summary: Apple has unveiled its next-generation M4 chip built on TSMC's 3nm process, featuring a 10-core CPU and up to 120 TOPS of neural engine performance.
source.content: Apple today announced the M4 chip, its most powerful silicon for consumer devices. Built on TSMC's second-generation 3-nanometer process, the M4 features a new 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores. The chip delivers up to 120 TOPS (trillions of operations per second) in its neural engine, making it Apple's most AI-capable chip to date. The M4 debuts in the new iPad Pro, with Mac integration expected later this year. Apple SVP of Hardware Technologies Johny Srouji called it a significant leap in power efficiency.

source.title: Microsoft Azure adds new AI services for enterprise customers
source.summary: Microsoft announced new Azure AI services including GPT-4 Turbo integration, custom model fine-tuning, and enhanced security features for enterprise deployments.
source.content: Microsoft expanded its Azure AI platform with three major additions aimed at enterprise customers. First, GPT-4 Turbo is now available through Azure OpenAI Service with 128K context windows and improved JSON mode. Second, enterprises can now fine-tune custom GPT-4 models using their proprietary data within Azure's secure environment. Third, Microsoft introduced Azure AI Content Safety, a new service that screens AI-generated content for harmful material before it reaches end users. Pricing starts at $0.01 per 1,000 tokens for GPT-4 Turbo. The features are available immediately in all Azure regions.
source.classification_reason: Primary: Enterprise (Azure services). Secondary: AI (GPT-4 integration).

source.title: Major data breach exposes 10 million customer records at fintech firm
source.summary: A fintech company disclosed a data breach affecting 10 million customers. Exposed data includes names, email addresses, and partial financial information. The breach was discovered by security researchers.
source.content: Fintech startup PayCore disclosed today that a data breach compromised the personal information of approximately 10 million customers. The breach, discovered by security firm CrowdStrike during a routine audit, exposed customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and the last four digits of bank account numbers. PayCore CEO Maria Chen said the company has hired Mandiant to lead the investigation and has notified affected customers. The breach occurred through a misconfigured API endpoint that was exposed for approximately three weeks between July 15 and August 5. No full financial credentials were compromised, according to the company.

source.title: Instagram launches AI-powered photo editing features
source.summary: Meta's Instagram is rolling out new AI-powered photo editing tools that can change backgrounds, adjust lighting, and generate creative filters using generative AI models.
source.content: Instagram announced today a suite of AI-powered editing tools built on Meta's generative AI models. The new features include AI Background, which can replace or modify photo backgrounds with text prompts; AI Enhance, which automatically adjusts lighting, color, and sharpness; and AI Filters, which generate custom artistic filters on demand. The tools are rolling out to all Instagram users globally over the next two weeks. Meta says the AI features run on its Llama-based vision models and process images on-device for privacy. Head of Instagram Adam Mosseri said the company has been testing the features with creators for three months.
source.classification_reason: Primary: Mobile & Apps (Instagram features). Secondary: AI (generative AI tools).

source.title: EU introduces new AI regulation requiring transparency in training data
source.summary: The European Union passed new regulations requiring AI companies to disclose their training data sources and implement content labeling for AI-generated media.
source.content: The European Parliament approved new AI transparency regulations that will require companies deploying AI systems in the EU to disclose the sources of their training data. The regulation, part of the EU AI Act implementation, mandates that general-purpose AI models like GPT-4 and Claude must provide summaries of copyrighted training material. Companies have 12 months to comply. Tech companies including OpenAI, Google, and Meta have expressed concerns about the feasibility of retroactively documenting all training data sources. The regulation also requires clear labeling of all AI-generated images, video, and audio content.
